inputs.doc: HEADPUB e043b-xl144-nolonhold-s0 · PUBLISHES the xl144 stage-2 head that #414 trained for the full 200,000 steps on the EXISTING frozen f3 anchor codec with the stage-2 pool opened to ALL longitudes (--train-lon-hold none, recipe xl144-nolonhold) · params 211.353M head (+ 40.693M frozen codec) · stage headpub (NOTHING trains; strips /opt/earth-cache/ckpt/temporal.pt to weights-only and uploads head-weights-e043b-xl144-nolonhold-s0.pt) · data family3_na025 (C 39, T 516) · arch 1024x16, K 24, stencil 145, ring spiral:111,4444,0.71,0.5, d_z 64 anchor geometry · steps x batch 200,000 x 256 stage-2 (= the checkpoint's own count; this job trains zero steps) · resume !run-62,run-63 (f3_anchor41M, frozen). WHY NOW: #414 finished its 200k steps and posted stage2_result (z_mse_model 0.04369 / persistence 3.13943, params_M 211.353, seed 0). The weights exist in exactly two places: /opt/earth-cache/ckpt/temporal.pt on gpu-box-30257785, and inside #414's own 30-day probes artifact zip -- neither of which any eval dispatch can consume. A published release asset is the only form a sroll can name, and an unpublished head is one box eviction from gone, which is what #396 taught. SOURCE PINNED TO @temporal deliberately, for the reason #412 recorded: a box's orphan-temporal-latest.pt can be a stale leftover, and publishing that leftover is what #377/#378/#381/#382 did. The printed step/d_model/layers/stencil/seed line must read step=200000 d_model=1024 layers=16 stencil=145 seed=0 znoise=0.0 and params=211.4M, and the checkpoint's args must carry train_lon_hold none, or the asset is the wrong file and must NOT be evaluated. The published asset is then the input to the E-043b sroll, whose corridor AUC against #418's xl144 split is the wave's holdout-effect measurement.
